title: Why U(8) is not cyclic
promptMarkdown:
In under 200 words and without the text open: explain why $U(8)$ is not cyclic, name the property that every cyclic group of order $4$ has and that $U(8)$ lacks, and relate the situation to exercise 1 of unit 1.

Then state, in one sentence each, whether $U(5)$ and $U(10)$ are cyclic, giving a generator and the list of its powers where one exists.
hintLadder: Compute $3^2$, $5^2$ and $7^2$ modulo $8$. What is the largest order of an element of $U(8)$?
A cyclic group of order $4$ contains an element of order $4$. Does $U(8)$?
$U(5)=\{1,2,3,4\}$ and $U(10)=\{1,3,7,9\}$; try the powers of $2$ and of $3$ respectively.

deterministicChecks.description: asserting that U(8) is cyclic (as a conclusion, not as a hypothesis for contradiction)

criteria.criterion: Every element of U(8) squares to 1, so no element has order 4; a cyclic group of order 4 has a generator of order 4; hence U(8) is not cyclic.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Computation and the missing property both stated.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: Correct conclusion with the computation but without naming the property, or vice versa.

criteria.criterion: Relates to unit 1 exercise 1: a group in which every element squares to the identity is abelian, and U(8) is such a group (so it is abelian for two reasons, and it is the smallest abelian non-cyclic example, the Klein four-group pattern of Z_2 × Z_2).
U(5) is cyclic, generated by 2 (powers 2, 4, 3, 1); U(10) is cyclic, generated by 3 (powers 3, 9, 7, 1). Other generators (3 for U(5); 7 for U(10)) are equally acceptable.

levels.label: met
levels.description: Both correct with generators and powers.

levels.label: partially met
levels.description: One correct, or generators without powers.

checkExamples.label: correct explanation
checkExamples.text: U(8) = {1, 3, 5, 7} and 3^2 = 5^2 = 7^2 = 1 mod 8, so every element has order at most 2, while a cyclic group of order 4 must contain an element of order 4; hence U(8) is not cyclic. U(5) is cyclic with generator 2 (powers 2, 4, 3, 1) and U(10) is cyclic with generator 3 (powers 3, 9, 7, 1).

checkExamples.label: proof by contradiction phrasing
checkExamples.text: Suppose U(8) is cyclic, generated by g. Then g has order 4, but 3^2 = 5^2 = 7^2 = 1 in U(8), a contradiction.

checkExamples.label: wrong claim
checkExamples.text: U(8) is cyclic, generated by 3, since 3 has order 4.
